extracted.intended_audience: school and college/university administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and policymakers (recipients of federal education funds)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on when and how recipients may offer and conduct informal resolution (mediation, restorative justice, arbitration, etc.) for allegations of sexual harassment under §106.45, including limits, notice, training, voluntariness, and record/confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary participation; no requirement or conditioning of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are explicitly prohibited from requiring the parties to participate in an informal resolution process or from requiring students or employees to waive their right to a formal §106.45 grievance process as a condition of enrollment, employment, or enjoyment of any other right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must be voluntary and written; recipients must not intimidate, threaten, coerce, or otherwise pressure parties into informal resolution. The Department declined to mandate that parties first confer with an advisor (or be provided one) but emphasizes that consent cannot be product of coercion or undue influence. Recipients may not make informal resolution a default; parties retain the right to have allegations resolved through formal grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution can be offered only after a formal complaint is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(9) revised to state that recipients may not offer informal resolution unless a formal complaint has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures parties understand the allegations at issue and their right to the formal grievance process before electing informal resolution. Recipients must provide the initial written notice of allegations before informal resolution and may not use informal processes to short-circuit formal complaint awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No informal resolution for allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are categorically prohibited from offering or facilitating an informal resolution process to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition was added because of concerns about power differentials and undue influence in employee–student contexts. Recipients retain discretion to use informal resolution for other sexual harassment allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator impartiality and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals facilitating informal resolution must be free from conflicts of interest and bias, and trained to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The anti-conflict, anti-bias, and training requirements of §106.45(b)(1)(iii) have been extended to informal resolution facilitators; they must receive the same training required for Title IX Coordinators, investigators, and decision-makers. Training must cover the definition of sexual harassment in §106.30, scope of the recipient's program/activity, how to conduct informal resolution processes, and how to serve impartially (including avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, or bias). Recipients may outsource to third-party providers but remain responsible for these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial written notice must describe available informal resolution processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial written notice of allegations sent to both parties must include information about any informal resolution processes the recipient has chosen to make available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must also inform parties of the requirements of the informal process and any consequences resulting from participating, including what records will be maintained or could be shared and confidentiality implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of records and confidentiality implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must disclose, in writing, what records would be maintained or could be shared in the informal resolution process and the confidentiality implications of participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although written notice is required, recipients retain discretion to determine which records are public records and which may remain confidential; the Department notes that the written notice itself could be kept confidential. This requirement is intended to put both parties on notice about privacy and potential disclosure of records and to allow recipients to craft confidentiality parameters appropriate for their chosen informal models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution processes must have reasonably prompt time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added this as a change to ensure informal processes proceed without undue delay; specific timelines are left to recipients to define consistent with the requirement of reasonable promptness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to withdraw prior to agreement; binding nature of agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party has the right to withdraw from informal resolution and resume the §106.45 grievance process at any time before agreeing to a resolution; where parties do agree, informal resolution agreements are expected to be treated as contracts and may be binding according to their terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects informal resolution agreements to clearly specify terms, and once entered they may include consequences for breach, though the final rule does not mandate specific breach-remedy provisions. The ability to withdraw prior to agreement addresses concerns about parties being trapped in informal processes and supports good-faith participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survivor-oriented protections are permitted but not mandated
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations decline to mandate specific survivor-oriented protections (e.g., prohibiting in-person questioning, requiring written submissions, or requiring safety/risk analyses), leaving these measures to recipient discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain flexibility to require safeguards such as parties being in separate rooms, a third party sitting in, prohibiting direct questioning, or performing a risk analysis before offering informal resolution. The Department declined to impose these as universal mandates to preserve recipient flexibility to meet community needs, although nothing in the regulations precludes adopting such protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restorative justice permitted as a form of informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use restorative justice models as an informal resolution option; restorative justice often requires a respondent's admission of responsibility but that admission does not necessarily equate to a recipient's determination of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in restorative justice must be voluntary. Recipients may specify whether a respondent's admission in restorative justice would be used in a later adjudication if a party withdraws from the informal process. A recipient also may use restorative justice after a formal determination of responsibility; the regulations do not dictate specific sanctioning forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not use informal resolution to avoid formal grievance obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not avoid implementing a formal resolution process by offering only informal resolution; formal grievance procedures under §106.45 must remain available and cannot be waived as condition of enrollment/employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.45(b)(9) to preclude recipients from requiring waivers of formal process rights and from making informal resolution the only avenue to resolve allegations, addressing concerns that some recipients might attempt to evade formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against institutional incentives and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Because recipients may have reputational or monetary incentives to prefer informal resolution, the regulations require safeguards—training, impartial facilitators, voluntariness, and prohibition on conditioning rights—to counteract such perverse incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes these cumulative requirements (impartial facilitators, written informed consent, ability to withdraw, prohibition on requiring participation, and disclosure obligations) will mitigate pressures that might otherwise push parties toward informal resolution for the institution's benefit rather than the parties'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to parents/guardians for minors or legally incompetent persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the complainant or respondent is a minor or legally incompetent person, the party's parent or legal guardian will receive the required written notice under §106.45(b)(9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added §106.6(g) to acknowledge parents' and guardians' legal rights to act on behalf of individuals exercising Title IX rights or involved in proceedings; notices and other rights apply accordingly.
